audit.why: Difficulty 4/10 FAVOURED matches a dashless scaling mage against a melee engage tank with a taunt and a global R; early/mid lane belongs to Galio, side lane and teamfight zone control is where Viktor claws back.
audit.corrected: Kept FAVOURED 4/10, but the Emerald+ win rate is 50.21% over 4473 games, which reads even rather than favoured — flagged in notes rather than flipping the chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes referenced 'Chaos Storm', 'Power Siphon' and 'Death Ray' — none of those are Viktor's ability names — and no real cooldowns anchored the spike text.
audit.why: Riot's kit gives Siphon Power (Q, 9/8/7/6/5), Gravity Field (W, 17/16/15/14/13), Hextech Ray (E, 12/11/10/9/8), Arcane Storm (R, 120/100/80). Galio spikes are level 3 (full rotation), level 6 (R at 4000/4750/5500 range) and first item.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten with the real names, the 120s rank-1 Arcane Storm, the 12s Hextech Ray clear and the 5500-unit rank-3 Hero's Entrance.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interactions were never stated: Siphon Power is an auto-attack reset (the wind-up is the tell), Siphon Power also grants Viktor a shield that eats the first half of your trade, and Viktor has no dash at all against a 650-range Justice Punch knockup into Shield of Durand's taunt.
audit.why: Kit flags: Viktor Q = shield + autoReset; Galio E = dash/knockup at 650 range, 11/10/9/8/7; Galio W = hardCC taunt + shield, 18/17/16/15/14; Galio R = knockup + shield at 4000/4750/5500.
audit.corrected: Trade advice now keys off the Q reset wind-up and the spent shield, and the engage advice states that Viktor has no escape once Justice Punch lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that must hold real numbers.
audit.corrected: Now carries Gravity Field 17s rank 1, Shield of Durand 18s rank 1, Hextech Ray 12s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page claims you can 'interrupt' or 'body-block' Viktor's ultimate cast.
audit.why: Riot's text says Arcane Storm interrupts ENEMY channels; nothing in the kit says the cast itself is interruptible, and the derived 'channel' flag looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire from that same sentence. Not asserting it either way.
audit.corrected: Replaced the interrupt claim with verified behaviour: it is a redirectable zone on a 120s rank-1 cooldown, so leave the ground it covers.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Shield of Durand has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Viktor Gravity Field: 17s at rank 1 — the stun zone owns every all-in, so walk out as it lands and step in while it is down. - Your W Shield of Durand is 18s at rank 1: spend it on his commit. - Hextech Ray is 12s — his only fast answer between them.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Galio's passive procs bonus magic damage in an area — walk up and trade after his Siphon Power shield is spent, not into it.

edits.before: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield.
edits.after: He has no dash: taunt when he walks up to Siphon Power a minion near you, not when he is already backing off with the shield up.

edits.before: Viktor whiffs Gravity Field and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance covers 4000 units — leave the wave when he shoves.

edits.before: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.
edits.after: E is your only gap-closer at 11s rank 1 — burn it on the wave and his 12s Hextech Ray pokes you free until it comes back.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Viktor wins by stunning you inside Gravity Field, chipping you with Hextech Ray, and scaling in a lane he never had to leave.

edits.before: Carry through arrivals — Hero's Entrance turns every losing skirmish your team starts into a 5v4 with a knockup.
edits.after: Carry by arriving — Viktor has no dash, so a Hero's Entrance on top of him leaves him walking out of your taunt range.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-cleared middle wave that keeps your R timer flexible — Galio waves are about being free to leave. Worst wave: a hard-shoved wave when your bot lane is fighting — the R you couldn't channel is the fight your team lost. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: a middle wave you can leave — Viktor clears with a 12s Hextech Ray, so match his clear and keep the R timer free. Worst wave: a wave frozen near his tower, where Gravity Field covers your only walk-out. Crash timing: crash before you roam, so his shove costs him the tempo instead of you.

edits.before: Level 3 favors you since your Justice Punch dash punishes his lack of escape whenever he commits to a Power Siphon.
edits.after: Level 3 favors you since your Justice Punch dash punishes his lack of escape whenever he steps up to Siphon Power a minion.

edits.before: Viktor's Siphon Power poke is telegraphed and slow to ramp, so you can walk up and threaten Justice Punch the moment he over-commits to a Power Siphon on minions near you.
edits.after: Viktor's Siphon Power is an auto-attack reset — the wind-up, not the cast, is your cue. Threaten Justice Punch the moment he steps up to reset it on a minion near you.

edits.before: Chaos Storm gives Viktor a strong teamfight zone tool, but its long cast time and stationary nature mean you can body-block or interrupt it with a well-timed Hero's Entrance before it fully deploys.
edits.after: Arcane Storm gives Viktor a teamfight zone tool on a 120s cooldown at rank 1, and he can redirect it — so fight where it is not and force him to spend it before your Hero's Entrance arrives on a fight.

edits.before: His first item spike (usually Hextech items) improves his poke and wave clear, but you still out-duel him at close range since his kit lacks any hard escape once Justice Punch lands.
edits.after: His first item improves his poke and wave clear, but he still has no dash, so you out-duel him at close range once Justice Punch lands and Shield of Durand eats the rest of his damage.

edits.before: Late game his Chaos Storm and Gravity Field zone control matter, but your Shield of Durand tanks the damage while your team collapses, and Hero's Entrance lets you dive him before he sets up safely.
edits.after: Late his Arcane Storm and Gravity Field zone the fight, but Shield of Durand eats the magic damage while your team collapses, and Hero's Entrance drops you on him from up to 5500 units away.

edits.before: You outclass Viktor for most of the laning phase — his kit is built around safe, ranged poke and scaling, but he has no dash and no hard escape, so once you close the gap with Justice Punch he's forced into a losing trade every time. Push the wave to deny his farm and punish any moment he commits to a long Power Siphon channel near the minion line. Watch for Gravity Field zoning but don't let it stop you from engaging when the field is down.
edits.after: You outclass Viktor for most of the laning phase — his kit is built around safe, ranged poke and scaling, but he has no dash and no hard escape, so once you close the gap with Justice Punch he's forced into a losing trade every time. Push the wave to deny his farm and punish the moment he steps up to Siphon Power a minion near you — that cast resets his auto, so the wind-up is your cue. Gravity Field is a 17s stun zone at rank 1: engage while it is down.

edits.before: Chaos Storm coming online at 6 gives Viktor a strong area-denial ultimate, but it has a long cast animation and doesn't move once placed, so you can often interrupt the setup or simply avoid standing in it while still winning the 1v1 engage. Keep applying lane pressure and don't let him free-farm to a full Hextech power spike uncontested.
edits.after: Arcane Storm at 6 gives Viktor area denial on a 120s cooldown at rank 1, and he can redirect it, so treat it as ground you leave rather than damage you tank — step out and make him chase you with it while your wave keeps rolling into his tower. Keep applying lane pressure and don't let him free-farm his first item; a 12s Hextech Ray is his only fast clear.

edits.before: Even with a completed build, Viktor's Chaos Storm and Gravity Field are strong from range but do little against a dive that starts with Hero's Entrance and ends with Justice Punch stun — his kit still lacks the mobility to disengage once you're on top of him. Focus him first in fights since removing him early neutralizes his zone control before it matters.
edits.after: Even with a completed build, Viktor's Arcane Storm and Gravity Field are strong from range but do little against a dive that starts with Hero's Entrance and ends with a Justice Punch knockup into taunt — he has no dash to disengage once you're on top of him. Focus him first in fights since removing him early neutralizes his zone control before it matters.

edits.before: Punish his Power Siphon animation by walking up and threatening Justice Punch the instant he commits
edits.after: Punish his Siphon Power auto reset by walking up and threatening Justice Punch the instant he winds up

edits.before: Body-block or flank his Chaos Storm cast with Hero's Entrance before it fully forms
edits.after: Leave the ground his Arcane Storm covers and make him redirect it away from your team

edits.before: Poke you down safely with Power Siphon and Death Ray from max range
edits.after: Poke you down safely with Siphon Power and Hextech Ray from max range

edits.before: Kite and disengage using Death Ray's slow rather than trading in melee range
edits.after: Kite with Gravity Field's slow and Hextech Ray chip, never trading in melee range

notes: Level chart left untouched (all seven rows Galio) — it matches packet.levelChart, but the Emerald+ win rate is 50.21% over 4473 games, which argues for an even matchup rather than a 7-0 sweep and a 4/10 difficulty. Flagged rather than flipped, per the chart rule. Also: the page repeatedly claimed you can interrupt or body-block Viktor's ultimate cast; Riot's text only says Arcane Storm interrupts enemy channels, and the kit's derived 'channel' flag appears to be a parse of that same sentence. I removed the claim rather than assert it either way. Fabricated names corrected throughout: Chaos Storm -> Arcane Storm, Power Siphon -> Siphon Power, Death Ray -> Hextech Ray. Hextech Ray has no slow in Riot's text (only the Gravity Field augment slows), so wants.foe[3] was regrounded.
